provenance.kind: Project-authored controlled scientific study. All tables are stipulated model observations, not a claim of new experimental or ab-initio results.
provenance.scope: Inference is conditional on the explicit finite model, source identities, units and measurement policy.

model: An exact finite-state Monte Carlo design problem. Choose one proposal q with q_j>0 and sum(q)=1. Each independent draw X~q contributes Y=p_X*f_X/q_X; the estimator is the arithmetic mean of Y over the fixed draw budget. Target p is normalized and known. This is ordinary unbiased importance sampling,not self-normalized importance sampling. All states have nonzero target contributions,so support cannot be dropped.
objective: Globally minimize the EXACT variance per importance draw over the full admissible probability simplex,then obtain the standard error of the unbiased sample-mean estimator. Compare with direct sampling q=p. A proposed q proportional to the signed p*f is admissible only if all probabilities are positive; negative contributions do not authorize negative sampling probabilities. A zero-variance assertion must satisfy both the estimator and admissible-support conditions.
scope: Controlled signed-contrast numerical integration and simulation allocation,not a finite-population survey,inverse-probability missing-response correction or empirical Monte Carlo run.
